title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 105 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 545–549 (Night 105, continuing directly from nights-104), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 105 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharrukān is buried, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān swears not to leave Constantinople until he has avenged him; he shares out the plundered treasure, sends money and letters home, and asks after the child his wife was expecting. Inside the city, Dhāt al-Dawāhī mourns the dead King Ḥardūb, here called her son, tells King Afrīdūn that she has killed Sharrukān and vows to kill the sultan and all his commanders, then has a letter shot into the Muslim camp confessing every crime. Ḍawʾ al-Makān swears a savage revenge and wastes with grief; the vizier Dandān consoles him with a verse; and news comes from Baghdad that the king's wife has borne a son, whom Nuzhat al-Zamān has named Kān Mā Kān. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and fifth night,
sentences.n: The print has الميلة, a misprint for الليلة (al-layla, “the night”), corrected here.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهُمْ جَهَّزُوا شَرْكَانَ وَدَفَنُوهُ فِى الْجَبَلِ الْمَذْكُورِ وَحَزِنُوا عَلَى فَضْلِهِ الْمَشْهُورِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahum jahhazū sharrukāna wa-dafanūhu fī al-jabali al-madhkūri wa-ḥazinū ʿalā faḍlihi al-mashhūri
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that they prepared Sharrukān, and buried him in the mountain mentioned, and grieved over his famed excellence.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that they laid out Sharrukān and buried him on the mountain already spoken of, and mourned his famous virtue.
sentences.n: Shahrazād opens the night by repeating, almost word for word, the sentence that closed the last one. The rhyme falls on al-madhkūr / al-mashhūr.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْتَظَرُوا بَابَ الْمَدِينَةِ أَنْ يُفْتَحَ فَمَا فُتِحَ وَلَا بَانَ لَهُمْ عَلَى الْأَسْوَارِ أَثَرُ أَحَدٍ فَتَعَجَّبُوا غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma intaẓarū bāba al-madīnati an yuftaḥa fa-mā futiḥa wa-lā bāna lahum ʿalā al-aswāri atharu aḥadin fa-taʿajjabū ghāyata al-ʿajabi
sentences.l: Then they waited-for the gate of the city, that it be opened; and it was not opened, nor appeared to them on the walls a trace of anyone; and they wondered the utmost of wonder.
sentences.i: Then they waited for the city gate to open; but it did not open, and not a sign of anyone showed on the walls, and they were utterly astonished.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَحُولُ عَنْهُمْ وَلَوْ أَقْعُدُ سِنِينَ وَأَعْوَامًا حَتَّى آخُذَ بِثَارِ أَخِي شَرْكَانَ وَأُخَرِّبَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ وَأَقْتُلَ مُلُوكَ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ وَلَوْ تُدْرِكُنِي الْمَنِيَّةُ وَأَسْتَرِيحُ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا الدَّنِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-allāhi lā aḥūlu ʿanhum wa-law aqʿudu sinīna wa-aʿwāman ḥattā ākhudha bi-thāri akhī sharrukāna wa-ukharriba al-qusṭanṭīniyyata wa-aqtula mulūka al-naṣrāniyyati wa-law tudrikunī al-maniyyatu wa-astarīḥu mina al-dunyā al-daniyyati
sentences.l: And King Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: By God, I will not turn from them, even if I sit years and years, until I take the blood-revenge of my brother Sharrukān, and lay-waste Constantinople, and kill the kings of Christendom — even if death overtakes me and I take-rest from the world the base.
sentences.i: King Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “By God, I will not leave them, though I sit here for years on end, until I have avenged my brother Sharrukān, laid Constantinople waste and killed the kings of Christendom — even if death overtakes me, and I find my rest from this mean world.”
sentences.n: akhadha bi-thār, “take (bi-) vengeance for”: thār is thaʾr, “blood-revenge”, with its hamza unwritten. al-dunyā al-daniyya, “the base world”, plays on the shared letters of the two words and rhymes with al-maniyya, “death”. law, “even if”, is followed by the plain present, as in the spoken language. The shaddas on المنيّة and الدنيّة are the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ الْأَمْوَالِ الَّتِي أَخَذُوهَا مِنْ دَيْرِ مَطْرُوحَنَى وَجَمَعَ الْعَسَاكِرَ وَفَرَّقَ الْأَمْوَالَ وَمَا تَرَكَ أَحَدًا حَتَّى أَعْطَاهُ وَاكْتِفَاءً مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-iḥḍāri al-amwāli allatī akhadhūhā min dayri maṭrūḥanā wa-jamaʿa al-ʿasākira wa-farraqa al-amwāla wa-mā taraka aḥadan ḥattā aʿṭāhu wa-iktifāʾan mina al-māli
sentences.l: Then he commanded the bringing of the riches which they had taken from the monastery of Maṭrūḥanā, and gathered the troops, and divided the riches; and he did not leave anyone but he gave him — and a sufficiency of the money.
sentences.i: Then he ordered the treasure they had taken from the monastery of Maṭrūḥanā to be brought, gathered the troops and shared the treasure out, and left no one without a gift, and enough money besides.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “command”: the verb takes the thing commanded with bi-. wa-iktifāʾan min al-māl, “and a sufficiency of money”, hangs loosely on aʿṭāhu, “he gave him”; the reading is ours, and the sense is plain enough: every man had all he needed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَحْضَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ طَائِفَةٍ ثَلٰثَمِائَةِ فَارِسٍ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ أَرْسِلُوا النَّفَقَاتِ إِلَى بُيُوتِكُمْ لِأَنِّي مُقِيمٌ هُنَا عَلَى هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ سِنِينَ وَأَعْوَامًا حَتَّى آخُذَ ثَارَ أَخِي شَرْكَانَ وَلَوْ أَمُوتُ فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma aḥḍara min kulli ṭāʾifatin thalāthamiʾati fārisin wa-qāla lahum arsilū al-nafaqāti ilā buyūtikum li-annī muqīmun hunā ʿalā hādhihi al-madīnati sinīna wa-aʿwāman ḥattā ākhudha thāra akhī sharrukāna wa-law amūtu fī hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: Then he brought-forward from each company three hundred horsemen and said to them: Send the expenses to your houses, for I am staying here over this city years and years until I take the blood-revenge of my brother Sharrukān, even if I die in this place.
sentences.i: Then he summoned three hundred horsemen from every company and said to them, “Send money home to your households for their keep, for I am staying here before this city for years on end until I have avenged my brother Sharrukān, even if I die in this place.”
sentences.n: ākhudha thāra akhī, “take my brother’s blood-revenge”: here thaʾr is the direct object, without the bi- of the sentence before last. The dagger alif in ثلٰثمائة is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ أَخَذُوا مَا أَعْطَاهُ لَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ وَأَجَابُوا بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ʿasākiru hādhā al-kalāma akhadhū mā aʿṭāhu lahum mina al-amwāli wa-ajābū bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati
sentences.l: And when the troops heard this speech, they took what he had given it to them of the riches, and answered with the hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: When the troops heard these words, they took the money he had given them and answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: mā aʿṭāhu lahum, “what he gave it to them”: the gift is marked twice, by -hu and by la-hum, a loose spoken construction.

sentences.t: وَأَحْضَرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ الْقُصَّادَ وَأَعْطَاهُمُ الْكُتُبَ وَأَوْصَاهُمْ بِإِيصَالِهَا وَإِيصَالِ الْأَمْوَالِ إِلَى بُيُوتِ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَأَنْ يُخْبِرُوهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ سَالِمُونَ مُطْمَئِنُّونَ
sentences.tr: wa-aḥḍara ḍawʾu al-makāni al-quṣṣāda wa-aʿṭāhumu al-kutuba wa-awṣāhum bi-īṣālihā wa-īṣāli al-amwāli ilā buyūti al-ʿasākiri wa-an yukhbirūhum bi-annahum sālimūna muṭmaʾinnūna
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān brought the couriers and gave them the letters, and charged them with the delivering of them, and the delivering of the riches to the houses of the troops, and that they tell them that they are safe, at-ease.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān summoned the couriers, gave them the letters and charged them to deliver them, and the money too, to the soldiers’ households, and to tell them that their men were safe and in good heart.
sentences.n: awṣāhum bi-, “charged them with”: the verb takes the charge with bi-; akhbara bi-, “tell (someone) of”. The shadda on القصّاد is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَأَعْلِمُوهُمْ أَنَّنَا فِي حِصَارِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ إِمَّا أَنْ نُخَرِّبَهَا أَوْ نَمُوتَ وَلَوْ أَقَمْنَا شُهُورًا وَأَعْوَامًا مَا نَرْحَلُ عَنْهَا إِلَّا بِفَتْحِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-aʿlimūhum annanā fī ḥiṣāri al-qusṭanṭīniyyati immā an nukharribahā aw namūta wa-law aqamnā shuhūran wa-aʿwāman mā narḥalu ʿanhā illā bi-fatḥihā
sentences.l: And inform-them that we are in the siege of Constantinople: either that we lay-it-waste or we die; and even if we stay months and years, we do not depart from it except with its conquest.
sentences.i: “And tell them that we are laying siege to Constantinople: either we lay it waste or we die; and though we stay for months and years, we will not leave it until it has fallen.”
sentences.n: The narrative slides straight into the king’s own words: aʿlimūhum, “inform them”, is his order to the couriers, with no “he said” before it. illā bi-fatḥihā, “except with (bi-) its conquest”. The shadda on نخرّبها is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ كِتَابًا إِلَى أُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَعْلِمْهَا بِمَا وَقَعَ لَنَا وَمَا نَحْنُ فِيهِ وَأَوْصِهَا بِوَلَدِي لِأَنِّي لَمَّا خَرَجْتُ كَانَتْ زَوْجَتِى قَرِيبَةً مِنَ الْوِلَادَةِ وَمَاهِيَ الْآنَ إِلَّاوَلَدَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-wazīra dandāna an yaktuba kitāban ilā ukhtihi nuzhati al-zamāni wa-qāla lahu aʿlimhā bi-mā waqaʿa lanā wa-mā naḥnu fīhi wa-awṣihā bi-waladī li-annī lammā kharajtu kānat zawjatī qarībatan mina al-wilādati wa-mā hiya al-āna illā waladat
sentences.l: Then he commanded the vizier Dandān that he write a letter to his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and said to him: Inform her of what has befallen us and what we are in, and charge her with my child; for when I went-out, my wife was near to the giving-birth, and she is not now except she has given-birth.
sentences.i: Then he told the vizier Dandān to write a letter to his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and said to him, “Tell her what has happened to us and how we stand, and commend my child to her care; for when I set out, my wife was near her time, and by now she must have given birth.
sentences.n: The print has زوحتى, a misprint for زوجتى (zawjatī, “my wife”), corrected here. “His sister” is the king’s: Nuzhat al-Zamān is Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s sister. awṣā bi-, “commend (to someone’s care)”. mā hiya al-āna illā waladat, “she is not now but she has given birth”: by now she cannot not have. ماهي and الاولدت are each printed as one word, and kept so.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَتْ رُزِقَتْ وَلَدًا كَمَا سَمِعْتُ فَأَسْرِعْ فِى الْعَوْدِ وَائْتِنِي بِالْأَخْبَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-in kānat ruziqat waladan kamā samiʿtu fa-asriʿ fī al-ʿawdi wa-iʾtinī bi-al-akhbāri
sentences.l: And if she has been granted a boy, as I heard, then hasten in the return and come-to-me with the news.
sentences.i: If she has been granted a son, as I have heard, then hurry back and bring me the news.”
sentences.n: ruziqat waladan, “she was granted (as God’s provision) a child”; walad here, as often, means a son. Who is to hurry back is not said: presumably the messenger who carries the letter. iʾtinī bi-, “come to me with”, that is, “bring me”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ وَهَبَهُمْ شَيْاً مِنَ الْمَالِ فَأَخَذُوةُ وَسَافَرُوا مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma wahabahum shayʾan mina al-māli fa-akhadhūhu wa-sāfarū min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi
sentences.l: Then he gifted them a thing of the money, and they took it and travelled from its time and its hour.
sentences.i: Then he gave them some money, and they took it and set out that very hour.
sentences.n: شيا is shayʾ, “a thing”, without its hamza; the tanwīn mark is the print’s. فاخذوة ends in ة for the pronoun -hu (akhadhūhu, “they took it”), a spelling this edition uses often. min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi, “from its time and its hour”: at once.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجَ النَّاسُ لِوَدَاعِهِمْ وَأَوْصَوْهُمْ عَلَى أَمْوَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaja al-nāsu li-wadāʿihim wa-awṣawhum ʿalā amwālihim
sentences.l: And the people went-out for the farewelling of them, and charged them over their riches.
sentences.i: The people came out to see them off, and charged them to take good care of their money.
sentences.n: li-wadāʿihim, “for (li-) bidding them farewell”. awṣā ʿalā, “charge with the care of”, where a few sentences back the same verb took bi-.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ مَسِيرِهِمْ أَقْبَلَ الْمَلِكُ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَأَمَرَةُ أَنْ يَأْمُرَ النَّاسَ بِالزَّحْفِ مِنْ قُرْبِ السُّورِ فَزَحَفُوا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا أَحَدًا عَلَى الْأَسْوَارِ فَتَعَجَّبُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda masīrihim aqbala al-maliku ʿalā al-wazīri dandāna wa-amarahu an yaʾmura al-nāsa bi-al-zaḥfi min qurbi al-sūri fa-zaḥafū fa-lam yajidū aḥadan ʿalā al-aswāri fa-taʿajjabū min dhālika
sentences.l: Then after their going, the king turned-to the vizier Dandān and commanded him that he command the people with the advancing from near the wall; and they advanced, and did not find anyone on the walls, and they wondered at that.
sentences.i: When they had gone, the king turned to the vizier Dandān and told him to order the men to advance close up to the wall. They advanced, found no one on the walls, and wondered at it.
sentences.n: وامرة has ة for -hu again (amarahu, “commanded him”). amara bi-, “order (something)”; zaḥf is an advance on the enemy.

sentences.t: وَبَقِيَ السُّلْطَانُ مَهْمُومًا لِذَلِكَ حَزِينًا عَلَى فِرَاقِ أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ مُتَحَيِّرًا عَلَى الزَّاهِدِ الْخَوَّانِ فَأَقَامُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَحَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-baqiya al-sulṭānu mahmūman li-dhālika ḥazīnan ʿalā firāqi akhīhi sharrukāna mutaḥayyiran ʿalā al-zāhidi al-khawwāni fa-aqāmū ʿalā dhālika thalāthata ayyāmin fa-lam yaraw aḥadan
sentences.l: And the sultan remained anxious for that, grieving over the parting of his brother Sharrukān, perplexed over the ascetic the traitor; and they stayed upon that three days, and did not see anyone.
sentences.i: The sultan stayed troubled by it, grieving at the loss of his brother Sharrukān and baffled over the treacherous ascetic; and so they waited three days, and saw no one.
sentences.n: The print has حزنيا, a misprint for حزينا (ḥazīnan, “grieving”), corrected here. li-dhālika, “for (li-) that”, “because of it”. The shadda on الخوّان is the print’s.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-muslimīna
sentences.l: This is what was of the affair of the Muslims.
sentences.i: So much for the Muslims.
sentences.n: ماكان is printed as one word, here and in the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الرُّومِ وَسَبَبِ غِيَابِهِمْ عَنِ الْقِتَالِ فِي هَذِةِ الثَّلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فَإِنَّ ذَاتَ الدَّوَاهِي لَمَّا قَتَلَتْ شَرْكَانَ أَسْرَعَتْ فِي مَشْيِهَا وَأَتَتْ إِلَى السُّورِ وَصَاحَتْ بِلِسَانِ الرُّومِ لِلْحُرَّاسِ أَنْ يُدْلُوا لَهَا الْحَبْلَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-rūmi wa-sababi ghiyābihim ʿani al-qitāli fī hādhihi al-thalāthati ayyāmin fa-inna dhāta al-dawāhī lammā qatalat sharrukāna asraʿat fī mashyihā wa-atat ilā al-sūri wa-ṣāḥat bi-lisāni al-rūmi li-al-ḥurrāsi an yudlū lahā al-ḥabla
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the Rūm, and the cause of their absence from the fighting in these three days: Dhāt al-Dawāhī, when she had killed Sharrukān, hastened in her walking, and came to the wall, and cried in the tongue of the Rūm to the guards that they let-down to her the rope.
sentences.i: As for the Rūm, and why they had kept from the fighting those three days: when Dhāt al-Dawāhī had killed Sharrukān, she hurried away to the wall and called up to the guards in Greek to let down the rope for her.
sentences.n: hādhihi al-thalāthati ayyām, “these three days”, puts the article on the number rather than on the counted noun, a common later usage; هذة has ة for ه, as printed. bi-lisān al-Rūm, “in (bi-) the tongue of the Rūm”: Greek. The shadda on الحرّاس is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا مَنْ أَنْتِ فَقَالَتْ أَنَا ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي فَعَرَفُوهَا وَأَدْلَوْا لَهَا الْحَبْلَ فَرَبَطَتْ نَفْسَهَا وَسَحَبُوهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā man anti fa-qālat anā dhātu al-dawāhī fa-ʿarafūhā wa-adlaw lahā al-ḥabla fa-rabaṭat nafsahā wa-saḥabūhā
sentences.l: And they said to her: Who are you? And she said: I am Dhāt al-Dawāhī. And they knew her and let-down to her the rope, and she tied herself, and they hauled her.
sentences.i: “Who are you?” they asked, and she said, “I am Dhāt al-Dawāhī.” They knew her and let the rope down, and she tied herself to it and they hauled her up.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ دَخَلَتْ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا هَذَا الَّذِي سَمِعْتُهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّ ابْنِي حَرْدُوبَ قُتِلَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalat ilayhim dakhalat ʿalā al-maliki afrīdūna fa-qālat lahu mā hādhā alladhī samiʿtuhu mina al-muslimīna fa-innahum qālū inna ibnī ḥardūba qutila
sentences.l: And when she arrived to them, she entered upon King Afrīdūn and said to him: What is this which I have heard from the Muslims? For they said that my son Ḥardūb was killed.
sentences.i: When she reached them she went in to King Afrīdūn and said to him, “What is this I have heard from the Muslims? They say that my son Ḥardūb has been killed.”
sentences.n: She already knows: in the last night Ḍawʾ al-Makān told Sharrukān of Ḥardūb’s death while she sat beside them disguised as the ascetic. Here, as usually in the tale, Ḥardūb is her son; the last night called him her father (والدها).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَصَاحَتْ وَبَكَتْ وَمَازَالَتْ تَبْكِى حَتَّى أَبْكَتْ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَمَنْ حَضَرَ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla naʿam fa-ṣāḥat wa-bakat wa-mā zālat tabkī ḥattā abkat afrīdūna wa-man ḥaḍara ʿindahu
sentences.l: And he said: Yes. And she cried-out and wept, and did not cease weeping until she made-weep Afrīdūn and whoever was present with him.
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said; and she shrieked and wept, and went on weeping until she had Afrīdūn and all who were with him in tears.
sentences.n: The print has انريدون, a misprint for افريدون (Afrīdūn), corrected here. ومازالت is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْلَمَتْ أَفْرِيدُونَ أَنَّهَا ذَبَحَتْ شَرْكَانَ وَثَلٰثِينَ مِنَ الْغِلْمَانِ فَفَرِحَ أَفْرِيدُونُ بِذَلِكَ وَشَكَرَهَا وَقَبَّلَ يَدَيْهَا وَدَعَى لَهَا بِالصَّبْرِ عَلَى وَلَدِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma aʿlamat afrīdūna annahā dhabaḥat sharrukāna wa-thalāthīna mina al-ghilmāni fa-fariḥa afrīdūnu bi-dhālika wa-shakarahā wa-qabbala yadayhā wa-daʿā lahā bi-al-ṣabri ʿalā waladihā
sentences.l: Then she informed Afrīdūn that she had slaughtered Sharrukān and thirty of the pages; and Afrīdūn rejoiced at that, and thanked her, and kissed her two-hands, and prayed for her with patience over her son.
sentences.i: Then she told Afrīdūn that she had cut the throats of Sharrukān and thirty of the pages. Afrīdūn was glad of it; he thanked her, kissed her hands, and prayed that she be given patience in her grief for her son.
sentences.n: daʿā lahā bi-al-ṣabr, “prayed for her for (bi-) patience”: bi- marks what is asked for. دعى is the print’s spelling of daʿā. The shadda on قبّل is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ إِنِّي لَمْ أَرْضَ بِقَتْلِ كَلْبٍ مِنْ كِلَابِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فِي ثَأْرِ مَلِكٍ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi innī lam arḍa bi-qatli kalbin min kilābi al-muslimīna fī thaʾri malikin min mulūki al-zamāni
sentences.l: And she said: By the right of the Messiah, I am not content with the killing of a dog of the dogs of the Muslims in the blood-revenge of a king of the kings of the age.
sentences.i: She said, “By the truth of the Messiah, I am not satisfied with killing one Muslim dog to avenge one of the kings of the age.
sentences.n: wa-ḥaqqi al-Masīḥ, “by the right (ḥaqq) of the Messiah”: an oath in the Muslim form, put in a Christian mouth. raḍiya bi-, “be content with”: the verb takes its object with bi-.

sentences.t: وَلَا بُدَّ أَنِّي أَعْمَلُ حِيلَةً وَأُدَبِّرُ مَكِيدَةً أَقْتُلُ بِهَا السُّلْطَانَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَالْحَاجِبَ وَرُسْتُمَ وَبَهْرَامَ وَعَشَرَةَ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَلَا تَرُوحُ رَاسُ وَلَدِى بِرَاسِ شَرْكَانَ وَلَا يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-lā budda annī aʿmalu ḥīlatan wa-udabbiru makīdatan aqtulu bihā al-sulṭāna ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-al-wazīra dandāna wa-al-ḥājiba wa-rustama wa-bahrāma wa-ʿasharata ālāfi fārisin min ʿaskari al-islāmi wa-lā tarūḥu rāsu waladī bi-rāsi sharrukāna wa-lā yakūnu dhālika abadan
sentences.l: And no escape: I will make a stratagem and contrive a plot by which I kill the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the vizier Dandān, and the chamberlain, and Rustam, and Bahrām, and ten thousand horsemen of the army of Islam; and the head of my son shall not go for the head of Sharrukān — and that shall never be.
sentences.i: I must devise a trick and lay a plot by which to kill the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the vizier Dandān, the chamberlain, Rustam, Bahrām and ten thousand horsemen of the army of Islam. My son’s head shall not be paid for with Sharrukān’s — that shall never be.”
sentences.n: lā budda annī aʿmalu, “no escape: I shall make”, where Classical has lā budda an aʿmala. tarūḥu rās waladī bi-rās Sharrukān, “my son’s head shall go for (bi-, in exchange for) Sharrukān’s head”: one life is not price enough for the other. rās is raʾs, “head”, with its hamza unwritten; it takes a feminine verb here, though the word is usually masculine. The shadda on ادبّر is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِلْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ اعْلَمْ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُقِيمَ عَلَى وَلَدِي الْأَحْزَانَ وَأَقْطَعَ الزُّنَّارَ وَأَكْسِرَ الصُّلْبَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-al-maliki afrīdūna iʿlam yā malika al-zamāni annī urīdu an uqīma ʿalā waladī al-aḥzāna wa-aqṭaʿa al-zunnāra wa-aksira al-ṣulbāna
sentences.l: Then she said to King Afrīdūn: Know, O king of the age, that I want to set-up over my son the griefs, and cut the girdle, and break the crosses.
sentences.i: Then she said to King Afrīdūn, “Know, O king of the age, that I mean to hold the rites of mourning for my son: to cut the girdle and break the crosses.”
sentences.n: The zunnār is the girdle Christians wore; cutting it and breaking crosses seem to be acts of mourning, perhaps a mourner turning even on the signs of her faith. aḥzān / ṣulbān rhyme. The shaddas on انّي and الزنّار are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَفْرِيدُونُ افْعَلِي مَا شِئْتِ فَإِنِّي لَا أُخَالِفُ لَكِ أَمْرًا وَلَوْ عَمِلْتِ حُزْنَكِ زَمَانًا طَوِيلًا لَكَانَ قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla afrīdūnu ifʿalī mā shiʾti fa-innī lā ukhālifu laki amran wa-law ʿamilti ḥuznaki zamānan ṭawīlan la-kāna qalīlan
sentences.l: And Afrīdūn said: Do what you wish, for I do not oppose to you a command; and if you made your grief a long time, it would be little.
sentences.i: Afrīdūn said, “Do as you please; I will not go against any wish of yours. If you mourned for a long time, it would still be too little.
sentences.n: ʿamilti ḥuznaki, “you made your grief”: ʿamila, “do, make”, stands in for a more specific verb, as so often in this text. The shadda on فانّي is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَوْ أَرَادُوا يُحَاصِرُونَا سِنِينَ وَأَعْوَامًا لَمْ يَنَالُوا مِنَّا أَرَبًا وَلَا يَنَالُهُمْ مِنَّا غَيْرُ التَّعَبِ وَالنَّصَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-muslimīna law arādū yuḥāṣirūnā sinīna wa-aʿwāman lam yanālū minnā araban wa-lā yanāluhum minnā ghayru al-taʿabi wa-al-naṣabi
sentences.l: For the Muslims, if they wanted to besiege us years and years, would not obtain from us a purpose, nor would reach them from us other than the toil and the weariness.
sentences.i: For if the Muslims chose to besiege us for years on end, they would get nothing they want from us, and nothing from us would come their way but toil and weariness.”
sentences.n: arādū yuḥāṣirūnā, “they wanted they-besiege-us”: the second verb follows without an, as in the spoken language. taʿab and naṣab, “toil and weariness”, are a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلْعُونَةَ لَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنَ الدَّاهِيَةِ الَّتِى عَمِلَتْهَا وَالْمَخَازِى الَّتِي لِنَفْسِهَا أَبْدَتْهَا أَخَذَتْ دَوَاةً وَقِرْطَاسًا وَكَتَبَتْ فِيهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ شَوَاهِي ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي إِلَى حَضْرَةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malʿūnata lammā faraghat mina al-dāhiyati allatī ʿamilathā wa-al-makhāzī allatī li-nafsihā abdathā akhadhat dawātan wa-qirṭāsan wa-katabat fīhi min ʿindi shawāhī dhāti al-dawāhī ilā ḥaḍrati al-muslimīna
sentences.l: Then the accursed-one, when she had finished from the calamity which she had made, and the infamies which of her own self she had shown, took an inkwell and paper and wrote in it: From with Shawāhī Dhāt al-Dawāhī to the presence of the Muslims.
sentences.i: Then, when the accursed woman had done with the calamity she had worked and the infamies she had shown herself capable of, she took an inkwell and paper and wrote on it: “From Shawāhī, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, to the company of the Muslims.
sentences.n: The rhyme falls on ʿamilathā / abdathā, and al-dāhiya, “the calamity”, puns on her name, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “Lady of Calamities”. Shawāhī is her own name. min ʿindi, “from with”, is the usual way a letter names its sender; ḥaḍra, “presence”, is the courteous address of the receiver.

sentences.t: اعْلَمُوا أَنِّي دَخَلْتُ بِلَادَكُمْ وَغَشَشْتُ بِلُؤْمِى كِرَامَكُمْ وَقَتَلْتُ سَابِقًا مَلِكَكُمْ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ فِي وَسْطِ قَصْرِهِ وَقَتَلْتُ أَيْضًا فِي وَقْعَةِ الشِّعْبِ وَالْمَغَارَةِ رَجُلًا كَثِيرًا وَآخِرُ مَنْ قَتَلْتُهُ شَرْكَانُ وَغِلْمَانُهُ
sentences.tr: iʿlamū annī dakhaltu bilādakum wa-ghashashtu bi-luʾmī kirāmakum wa-qataltu sābiqan malikakum ʿumara bna al-nuʿmāni fī wasṭi qaṣrihi wa-qataltu ayḍan fī waqʿati al-shiʿbi wa-al-maghārati rajulan kathīran wa-ākhiru man qataltuhu sharrukānu wa-ghilmānuhu
sentences.l: Know that I entered your lands and cheated, by my baseness, your noble-ones; and I killed formerly your king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān in the middle of his palace; and I killed also, in the battle of the ravine and the cave, man many; and the last whom I killed is Sharrukān and his pages.
sentences.i: Know that I came into your lands and with my baseness deceived your noblest men. Before this I killed your king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān in the heart of his own palace; in the battle of the ravine and the cave I killed a great many men as well; and the last I have killed are Sharrukān and his pages.
sentences.n: bi-luʾmī, “by (bi-) my baseness”: luʾm, “baseness”, is set against kirām, “the noble”. rajulan kathīran, “man many”, is a singular for a multitude, as in the spoken language. The battle of the ravine and the cave is the fighting told in the nights before, when the Muslims were trapped in the mountains.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ سَاعَدَنِي الزَّمَانُ وَطَاوَعَنِي الشَّيْطَانُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ قَتْلِ السُّلْطَانِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-law sāʿadanī al-zamānu wa-ṭāwaʿanī al-shayṭānu lā budda min qatli al-sulṭāni wa-al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: And if the time aids me and Satan obeys me, there is no escape from the killing of the sultan and the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: If fortune helps me and Satan does my bidding, the sultan and the vizier Dandān shall surely die too.
sentences.n: The rhyme runs zamān / shayṭān / sulṭān / Dandān. لابد is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا الَّذِي أَتَيْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ فِي زِيِّ الزَّاهِدِ وَانْطَلَقَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنِّى الْحِيَلُ وَالْمَكَائِدُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā alladhī ataytu ilaykum fī ziyyi al-zāhidi wa-inṭalaqat ʿalaykum minnī al-ḥiyalu wa-al-makāʾidu
sentences.l: And I am the-one-who came to you in the garb of the ascetic, and there went-off upon you from me the tricks and the plots.
sentences.i: I am the one who came to you dressed as the ascetic, and my tricks and plots took you in.
sentences.n: alladhī, “the one who”, is the masculine form, though a woman writes it: the speaker is the man you saw. inṭalaqat ʿalaykum, “were let loose upon you”, that is, worked on you. The shadda on زيّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ سَلَامَتَكُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَارْحَلُوا وَإِنْ شِئْتُمْ هَلَاكَ أَنْفُسِكُمْ نَعَنِ الْإِقَامَةِ لَا تَعْدِلُوا فَلَوْ أَقَمْتُمْ سِنِينَ وَأَعْوَامًا فَمَا تَبْلُغُونَ مِنَّا مَرَامًا وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-in shiʾtum salāmatakum baʿda dhālika fa-irḥalū wa-in shiʾtum halāka anfusikum naʿani al-iqāmati lā taʿdilū fa-law aqamtum sinīna wa-aʿwāman fa-mā tablughūna minnā marāman wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: So if you wish your safety after that, then depart; and if you wish the destruction of your souls, (then) from the staying do not swerve; for if you stayed years and years, you would not reach from us an aim. And the peace.
sentences.i: So if you want to save yourselves after this, go; and if you want your own destruction, do not stir from where you are: for though you stay for years on end, you will get nothing you seek from us. Farewell.”
sentences.n: نعن is as printed and makes no sense as it stands; the sense wants فعن (fa-ʿani, “then from”) or وعن, “do not turn aside from staying”, and it is translated so. aʿwām / marām rhyme. wa-al-salām, “and peace”, is the formal close of a letter.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ أَنْ كَتَبَتِ الْكِتَابَ أَقَامَتْ فِي حُزْنِهَا عَلَى الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ دَعَتْ بِطْرِيقًا وَأَمَرَتْهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ الْوَرَقَةَ وَيَضَعَهَا فِي سَهْمٍ وَيَرْمِيَهَا إِلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda an katabati al-kitāba aqāmat fī ḥuznihā ʿalā al-maliki ḥardūba thalāthata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi daʿat biṭrīqan wa-amarathu an yaʾkhudha al-waraqata wa-yaḍaʿahā fī sahmin wa-yarmiyahā ilā al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And after she wrote the letter, she stayed in her grief over King Ḥardūb three days; and on the day the fourth she called a patrician and commanded him that he take the leaf and put it in an arrow and shoot it to the Muslims.
sentences.i: When she had written the letter, she kept up her mourning for King Ḥardūb for three days; and on the fourth day she called a patrician and told him to take the sheet, fix it to an arrow and shoot it over to the Muslims.
sentences.n: biṭrīq, from Latin patricius, through Greek patrikios, is the Arabic word for a Byzantine commander.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتِ الْكَنِيسَهَ وَصَارَتْ تَنْدُبُ وَتَبْكِي عَلَى فَقْدِ وَلَدِهَا وَقَالَتْ لِمَنْ تَسَلْطَنَ بَعْدَةُ لَابُدَّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَجَمِيعَ أُمَرَاءِ الْإِسْلَامِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalati al-kanīsata wa-ṣārat tandubu wa-tabkī ʿalā faqdi waladihā wa-qālat li-man tasalṭana baʿdahu lā budda an aqtula ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-jamīʿa umarāʾi al-islāmi
sentences.l: Then she entered the church and began lamenting and weeping over the loss of her son, and said to whoever became-sultan after him: No escape — I will kill Ḍawʾ al-Makān and all the emirs of Islam.
sentences.i: Then she went into the church and began to lament and weep for the son she had lost, and she said to the man who had become sultan after him, “I must kill Ḍawʾ al-Makān and every emir of Islam.”
sentences.n: الكنيسه ends in ه for ة, and بعدة in ة for the pronoun -hu, both as printed. tasalṭana, “became sultan”, is a late verb made from sulṭān; the text does not say who succeeded Ḥardūb.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amrihā
sentences.l: This is what was of her affair.
sentences.i: So much for her.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنَّهُمْ أَقَامُوا ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فِي هَمٍّ وَاغْتِمَامٍ وَفِي الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ نَظَرُوا إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ السُّورِ وَإِذَا بِبِطْرِيقٍ مَعَهُ سَهْمُ نُشَّابٍ وَفِي طَرَفِهِ كِتَابٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-muslimīna fa-innahum aqāmū thalāthata ayyāmin fī hammin wa-ightimāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi naẓarū ilā nāḥiyati al-sūri wa-idhā bi-biṭrīqin maʿahu sahmu nushshābin wa-fī ṭarafihi kitābun
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the Muslims, they stayed three days in care and sorrowing; and on the day the fourth they looked toward the side of the wall, and behold, a patrician, with him an arrow-shaft of arrows, and at its tip a letter.
sentences.i: As for the Muslims, they spent three days in care and gloom; and on the fourth day they looked over towards the wall, and there was a patrician holding an arrow, with a letter at its tip.
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-biṭrīq, “and behold, a patrician”: after idhā of surprise, bi- only marks what appears. hamm and ightimām, “care and sorrowing”, are a rhyming pair of one root. sahm nushshāb, “a shaft of arrows”: nushshāb is the collective, so simply “an arrow”.

sentences.t: فَصَبَرُوا عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى رَمَاةُ إِلَيْهِمْ فَأَمَرَ السُّلْطَانُ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabarū ʿalayhi ḥattā ramāhu ilayhim fa-amara al-sulṭānu al-wazīra dandāna an yaqraʾahu
sentences.l: And they were-patient with him until he shot it to them; and the sultan commanded the vizier Dandān that he read it.
sentences.i: They waited for him until he had shot it over to them, and the sultan told the vizier Dandān to read it.
sentences.n: رماة has ة for -hu again (ramāhu, “he shot it”).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَةُ وَسَمِعَ مَا فِيهِ وَعَرَفَ مَعْنَاهُ هَمَلَتْ بِالدُّمُوعِ عَيْنَاهُ وَصَاحَ وَتَضَجَّرَ مِنْ مَكْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾahu wa-samiʿa mā fīhi wa-ʿarafa maʿnāhu hamalat bi-al-dumūʿi ʿaynāhu wa-ṣāḥa wa-taḍajjara min makrihā
sentences.l: And when he read it and heard what was in it and knew its meaning, his two-eyes flowed with the tears, and he cried-out and chafed at her cunning.
sentences.i: When he had read it, heard what was in it and grasped its meaning, his eyes ran with tears, and he cried out in anguish at her cunning.
sentences.n: maʿnāhu / ʿaynāhu rhyme. hamalat bi-al-dumūʿ, “overflowed with (bi-) tears”. قرأة has ة for -hu, and the shadda on تضجّر is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ كَانَ قَلْبِي نَافِرًا مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-wazīru wa-allāhi la-qad kāna qalbī nāfiran minhā
sentences.l: And the vizier said: By God, my heart had been shying from her.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “By God, my heart always shied away from her.”
sentences.n: He said as much in the last night, when Sharrukān was found dead: his heart had shied from the ascetic from first to last.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السُّلْطَانُ وَهَذِةِ الْعَاهِرَةُ كَيْفَ عَمِلَتْ عَلَيْنَا الْحِيلَةَ مَرَّتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-sulṭānu wa-hādhihi al-ʿāhiratu kayfa ʿamilat ʿalaynā al-ḥīlata marratayni
sentences.l: And the sultan said: And this harlot — how did she work upon us the trick twice?
sentences.i: The sultan said, “And this whore — how did she manage to trick us twice?
sentences.n: Twice: most likely King ʿUmar’s death and now Sharrukān’s, though the ambush in the ravine was her work too. هذة has ة for ه; the shadda on مرّتين is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَحُولُ مِنْ هُنَا حَتَّى أَمْلَأَ فَرْجَهَا بِمَسِيحِ الرَّصَاصِ وَأَسْجُنَهَا سِجْنَ الطَّيْرِ فِي الْأَقْفَاصِ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَرْبِطُهَا مِنْ شَعْرِهَا وَأُصَلِّبُهَا عَلَى بَابِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin wa-allāhi lā aḥūlu min hunā ḥattā amlaʾa farjahā bi-masīḥi al-raṣāṣi wa-asjunahā sijna al-ṭayri fī al-aqfāṣi wa-baʿda dhālika arbiṭuhā min shaʿrihā wa-uṣallibuhā ʿalā bābi al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: But by God, I will not move from here until I fill her vulva with the molten of the lead, and imprison her the imprisoning of the birds in the cages; and after that I tie her by her hair and crucify her on the gate of Constantinople.
sentences.i: But by God, I will not move from here until I have filled her sex with molten lead and caged her as birds are caged; and after that I will tie her up by her hair and crucify her on the gate of Constantinople.”
sentences.n: masīḥ al-raṣāṣ, “the molten of lead”, read from sāḥa, “flow, melt”; the fatḥa on the mīm is the print’s. In its letters the word is al-Masīḥ, “the Messiah”, which may or may not be meant to sting. raṣāṣ / aqfāṣ rhyme. The shadda on اصلّبها is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرَ أَخَاةُ فَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: thumma tadhakkara akhāhu fa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: Then he remembered his brother and wept a weeping severe.
sentences.i: Then he remembered his brother, and wept bitterly.
sentences.n: اخاة has ة for -hu (akhāhu, “his brother”); the shadda on تذكّر is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْكُفَّارَ لَمَّا تَوَجَّهَتْ لَهُمْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي وَأَخْبَرَتْهُمْ بِمَا حَصَلَ فَرِحُوا بِقَتْلِ شَرْكَانَ وَسَلَامَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-kuffāra lammā tawajjahat lahum dhātu al-dawāhī wa-akhbarathum bi-mā ḥaṣala fariḥū bi-qatli sharrukāna wa-salāmati dhāti al-dawāhī
sentences.l: Then the unbelievers, when Dhāt al-Dawāhī turned to them and told them of what had happened, rejoiced at the killing of Sharrukān and the safety of Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.i: As for the unbelievers: when Dhāt al-Dawāhī came back to them and told them what had happened, they rejoiced at Sharrukān’s death and at her safe return.
sentences.n: The story steps back here to the night of her return, told above. fariḥa bi-, “rejoice at”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ رَجَعُوا عَلَى بَابِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَوَعَدَهُمُ السُّلْطَانُ أَنَّهُ إِنْ فَتَحَ الْمَدِينَةَ فَرَّقَ أَمْوَالَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ بِالسَّوِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-muslimīna rajaʿū ʿalā bābi al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-waʿadahumu al-sulṭānu annahu in fataḥa al-madīnata farraqa amwālahā ʿalayhim bi-al-sawiyyati
sentences.l: Then the Muslims returned upon the gate of Constantinople, and the sultan promised them that, if he conquered the city, he would divide its riches upon them with the equality.
sentences.i: Then the Muslims went back against the gate of Constantinople, and the sultan promised them that if he took the city he would share its wealth out among them equally.
sentences.n: bi-al-sawiyya, “with (bi-) equality”: in equal shares.

sentences.t: هَذَا وَالسُّلْطَانُ لَمْ تَنْشَفْ دُمُوعُهُ حُزْنًا عَلَى أَخِيهِ وَعَرَى جِسْمَهُ الْهُزَالُ حَتَّى صَارَ كَالْخِلَالِ
sentences.tr: hādhā wa-al-sulṭānu lam tanshaf dumūʿuhu ḥuznan ʿalā akhīhi wa-ʿarā jismahu al-huzālu ḥattā ṣāra ka-al-khilāli
sentences.l: This — and the sultan, his tears did not dry, in grief over his brother, and the wasting befell his body until he became like the toothpick.
sentences.i: All this while the sultan’s tears never dried, so grieved was he for his brother, and his body wasted until he was as thin as a toothpick.
sentences.n: hādhā wa-, “this, while …”, is a storyteller’s link: “meanwhile”. ʿarā, “befall”, is written عرى. ka-al-khilāl, “like (ka-) the toothpick”, a stock figure for thinness, rhymes with huzāl, “wasting”.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا فَإِنَّ أَخَاكَ مَا مَاتَ إِلَّا بِأَجَلِهِ وَلَيْسَ فِي هَذَا الْحُزْنِ فَائِدَةٌ وَمَا أَحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalayhi al-wazīru dandānu wa-qāla lahu ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-inna akhāka mā māta illā bi-ajalihi wa-laysa fī hādhā al-ḥuzni fāʾidatun wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān entered upon him and said to him: Be good of soul and cool of eye, for your brother did not die except by his appointed-term, and there is not in this grief a profit; and how beautiful is the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān went in to him and said, “Take heart and be comforted: your brother died only when his appointed hour came, and there is nothing to be gained by this grief. How well the poet put it:
sentences.n: ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan, “be good in soul and cool in eye”, the stock words of comfort. bi-ajalihi, “by (bi-) his term”: the hour of death fixed for every man. The shadda on قرّ is the print’s.

sentences.t:
مَالَا يَكُوْنُ فَلَا يَكُوْنُ بِحِيْلَة * اَبَدًا وَمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ فَيَكُوْنُ
سَيَكُوْنُ مَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ فِيْ وَقْتِهِ * وَاَخُ الْجَهَالَةِ دَائِمًا مَغْبُوْنُ
sentences.tr:
mā lā yakūnu fa-lā yakūnu bi-ḥīlatin * abadan wa-mā huwa kāʾinun fa-yakūnu
sa-yakūnu mā huwa kāʾinun fī waqtihi * wa-akhu al-jahālati dāʾiman maghbūnu
sentences.l:
What-is-not to be, it will not be by a stratagem, ever; and what is to-be, it will be.
It will be — what is to-be — in its time; and the brother of ignorance is always cheated.
sentences.i:
What is not to be will never come about by any scheme; and what is to be, will be.
What is to be will come, in its own time; and the fool is forever the loser.
sentences.n: The verse is pointed as printed; ḥīlatin is read for the metre, though the print has no tanwīn. مالا is mā lā, “what … not”, printed as one word. akhu al-jahāla, “the brother of ignorance”, is the ignorant man; the print gives akhu its short vowel. maghbūn, “cheated”, is the loser in a bargain.

sentences.t: فَدَعِ الْبُكَاءَ وَالنُّوَاحَ وَقَوِّ قَلْبَكَ لِحَمْلِ السِّلَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-daʿi al-bukāʾa wa-al-nuwāḥa wa-qawwi qalbaka li-ḥamli al-silāḥi
sentences.l: So leave the weeping and the wailing, and strengthen your heart for the carrying of the weapons.
sentences.i: So leave off weeping and wailing, and steel your heart to bear arms.”
sentences.n: nuwāḥ / silāḥ rhyme; li-ḥaml, “for (li-) carrying”. The marks on قوِّ are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَزِيرُ إِنَّ قَلْبِي مَهْمُومٌ مِنْ أَجْلِ مَوْتِ أَبِي وَأَخِي وَمِنْ أَجْلِ غِيَابِنَا عَنْ بِلَادِنَا فَإِنَّ خَاطِرِي مَشْغُولٌ بِرَعِيَّتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā wazīru inna qalbī mahmūmun min ajli mawti abī wa-akhī wa-min ajli ghiyābinā ʿan bilādinā fa-inna khāṭirī mashghūlun bi-raʿiyyatī
sentences.l: And he said: O vizier, my heart is troubled because of the death of my father and my brother, and because of our absence from our lands; for my mind is busy with my subjects.
sentences.i: He said, “Vizier, my heart is heavy for the deaths of my father and my brother, and because we are so far from home; my thoughts are with my people.”
sentences.n: mashghūl bi-, “taken up with”; khāṭir is the mind, one’s thoughts.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى الْوَزِيرُ هُوَ وَالْحَاضِرُونَ وَمَا زَالُوا مُقِيمِينَ عَلَى حِصَارِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā al-wazīru huwa wa-al-ḥāḍirūna wa-mā zālū muqīmīna ʿalā ḥiṣāri al-qusṭanṭīniyyati muddatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: And the vizier wept, he and the present-ones; and they did not cease staying at the siege of Constantinople a stretch of the time.
sentences.i: The vizier wept, and all who were there with him; and they kept up the siege of Constantinople for some time.
sentences.n: bakā al-wazīru huwa wa-, “the vizier wept, he and …”: the pronoun is repeated so that others can be joined to the subject.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِالْأَخْبَارِ وَرَدَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بَغْدَادَ صُحْبَةَ أَمِيرٍ مِنْ أُمَرَائِهِ مَضْمُونُهُ أَنَّ زَوْجَةَ الْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ رُزِقَتْ وَلَدًا وَسَمَّتْهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ أُخْتُ الْمَلِكِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum kadhālika wa-idhā bi-al-akhbāri waradat ʿalayhim min baghdāda ṣuḥbata amīrin min umarāʾihi maḍmūnuhu anna zawjata al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni ruziqat waladan wa-sammathu nuzhatu al-zamāni ukhtu al-maliki kāna mā kāna
sentences.l: And while they were thus, behold, the news arrived to them from Baghdad, in the company of an emir of his emirs, its purport that the wife of King Ḍawʾ al-Makān had been granted a boy, and Nuzhat al-Zamān, the sister of the king, named him Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: While they were so, news reached them from Baghdad, brought by one of the king’s emirs. The gist of it was that King Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s wife had been granted a son, and that Nuzhat al-Zamān, the king’s sister, had named him Kān Mā Kān;
sentences.n: Kān Mā Kān means “what was, was”, or “there came what came”. wa-idhā bi-al-akhbār, “and behold, the news”: bi- after idhā only marks what appears. maḍmūnuhu, “its content”, is masculine, probably thinking of the letter rather than the news. فبينماهم is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّ هَذَا الْغُلَامَ سَيَكُونُ لَهُ شَانٌ بِسَبَبِ مَا رَأَوْةُ لَهُ مِنَ الْعَجَائِبِ وَالْغَرَائِبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinna hādhā al-ghulāma sa-yakūnu lahu shānun bi-sababi mā raʾawhu lahu mina al-ʿajāʾibi wa-al-gharāʾibi
sentences.l: but this boy will have a standing, on account of what they saw of him of the wonders and the marvels.
sentences.i: and this boy will be someone of great consequence, for the wonders and marvels they have seen in him.
sentences.n: shān is shaʾn, “standing, importance”, with its hamza unwritten; رأوة has ة for -hu (raʾawhu, “they saw it”). lākinna, “but”, is hardly more than “and” here.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَمَرَتِ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَالْخُطَبَاءَ أَنْ يَدْعُوا لَكُمْ عَلَى الْمَنَابِرِ وَدُبُرَ كُلِّ صَلٰوةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qad amarati al-ʿulamāʾa wa-al-khuṭabāʾa an yadʿū lakum ʿalā al-manābiri wa-dubura kulli ṣalātin
sentences.l: And she has commanded the learned and the preachers that they pray for you on the pulpits and at the back of every prayer;
sentences.i: She has ordered the scholars and the preachers to pray for you from the pulpits and at the end of every prayer;
sentences.n: dubura kulli ṣalāt, “at the back of every prayer”: when it is finished. The dagger alif in صلٰوة is the print’s.

sentences.t: وَأَنَّنَا طَيِّبُونَ بِخَيْرٍ وَالْأَمْطَارُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَأَنَّ صَاحِبَكَ الْوَقَّادَ فِي غَايَةِ النِّعْمَةِ الْجَزِيلَةِ وَعِنْدَةُ الْخَدَمُ وَالْغِلْمَانُ وَلَكِنَّهُ إِلَى الْآنَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِمَا جَرَى لَكَ وَالسَّلَامُ
sentences.tr: wa-annanā ṭayyibūna bi-khayrin wa-al-amṭāru kathīratun wa-anna ṣāḥibaka al-waqqāda fī ghāyati al-niʿmati al-jazīlati wa-ʿindahu al-khadamu wa-al-ghilmānu wa-lākinnahu ilā al-āna lam yaʿlam bi-mā jarā laka wa-al-salāmu
sentences.l: and that we are well, in good, and the rains are many; and that your friend the stoker is in the utmost of the ample bounty, and with him are the servants and the pages; but he until now does not know of what has happened to you. And the peace.
sentences.i: that all is well with us, and the rains have been plentiful; and that your friend the stoker lives in the greatest comfort, with servants and pages about him, though he still does not know what has befallen you. Farewell.
sentences.n: The letter is given half in report, half in its own words: “we”, “your friend”. The stoker is the bath-stoker who took in Ḍawʾ al-Makān when he was a sick and penniless stranger, earlier in the tale. bi-khayr, “in (bi-) good”: well. وعندة has ة for -hu; the shaddas on طيّبون and الوقّاد are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ الْآنَ اشْتَدَّ ظَهْرِي حَيْثُ رُزِقْتُ وَلَدًا اسْمُهُ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni al-āna ishtadda ẓahrī ḥaythu ruziqtu waladan ismuhu kāna mā kāna
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Now my back has grown-strong, since I have been granted a boy whose name is Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “Now my back is strong again, for I have been granted a son, and his name is Kān Mā Kān.”
sentences.n: ishtadda ẓahrī, “my back has grown strong”: a son is a man’s support. ḥaythu, “where”, is used for “since, because”, as often in the later language.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
